marks.gloss_en: if R' Yosei would be followed even were his words kabbala and theirs Torah, all the more so now that his are Torah and theirs kabbala

Rebbi: had their words been words of Torah and the Distinguished One's words of kabbala, we would listen to the Distinguished One -- all the more so now that theirs are words of kabbala and his words of Torah
אמר קרא עשויות -- five that perform two mitzvot
say [the two mitzvot are] the firstborn and the gifts?
Rav Kahana: the verse says 'asuyot' -- [five] that perform two mitzvot: the first shearing and the gifts
עשויות -- five make their owner perform the mitzva
אלא אמר רב אשי: עשויות -- שמעשות את בעליהן ואומרות לו קום עשה מצוה (= p_ashi_asuyot_measot_baaleihen)
בכורה, חדא מי לא מיחייבא? -- a single animal is already obligated in the firstborn (= p_bechora_chada_mechayeva)
ולטעמיך, מתנות, חדא מי לא מיחייבא? -- by that reasoning the gifts too apply to a single animal
the firstborn -- is a single [animal] not obligated?
שנאמר וארבע צאן תחת השה -- four are called tzon
R' Yosei (via his son R' Yishmael): four
granted for Beit Shammai, two are also called tzon; but for Beit Hillel, what is the reason?
granted for Beit Shammai: two are also called 'tzon'
but the Master said: a third decision does not decide!
a third decision does not decide
אתיא גיזה גיזה: 'the first shearing of your flock you shall give him' (Deut 18:4) / 'and he was warmed with the shearing of my sheep [kevasai]' (Job 31:20) -- as there sheep, so here sheep
from where? Rav Chisda: it comes [by gezera shava] 'shearing' / 'shearing'
ונילף גיזה גיזה מבכור -- learn 'shearing' from the firstborn instead, whose shearing ban applies to the ox too (דתניא ... לא תעבוד ולא תגוז, 137a.4-5 = p_bechor_zeh_bazeh)
אמר קרא תתן לו -- ולא לשקו (= p_titen_lo_velo_lesako)
the verse says 'you shall give him' -- and not for his sack
כדאמר רבי יהושע בן לוי: לעמוד לשרת -- דבר הראוי לשירות; הכא נמי
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: 'to stand to serve' (Deut 18:5) -- a thing fit for service
שנאמר ומגז כבשי יתחמם
the school of R' Yishmael: sheep whose wool is hard are exempt from the first shearing
דתניא: לקט קצירך ולא לקט קיטוף; רבי יוסי אומר: אין לקט אלא הבא מחמת קציר
'the gleaning of your harvest' (Lev 23:22) -- and not the gleaning of picking
דתניא: רבי יוסי אומר: קציר -- אין לי אלא קציר, עוקר מנין? ת״ל לקצור; תולש מנין? ת״ל בקוצרך
R' Yosei: 'harvest' -- I have only harvest; one who uproots, from where? the verse says 'to reap'; one who plucks, from where? the verse says 'when you reap'
אף אנן נמי תנינא: מלבנות בצלים שבין הירק -- רבי יוסי אומר: פאה מכל אחד ואחד
beds of onions among vegetables -- R' Yosei: pe'a from each one
תני חדא: שוטף את הרחלים פטור; ותניא אידך: שוטף את הרחלים חייב -- the baraitot contradict
לא קשיא: הא רבנן, והא רבי יוסי (= p_shotef_chayav_rabbanan, p_shotef_patur_ryosei)
one who shears goats is exempt

the baraita: 'you shall not work with the firstborn of your ox nor shear the firstborn of your flock' (Deut 15:19) -- I have only ox in work and flock in shearing; from where to apply what is said of each to the other? the verse says 'you shall not work ... and you shall not shear'
we require shearing, and there is none [with goats' hair]
who did you hear holds this reasoning? R' Yosei
it is all R' Yosei, and this is what it teaches: [not the gleaning of picking] for R' Yosei says gleaning is only what comes by harvest
